questions.q: Which license is required to use Privileged Identity Management?
options: Microsoft Entra ID Free
Microsoft Entra ID P1, which includes Privileged Identity Management for eligible users
Microsoft Entra Workload Identities Premium
Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra ID Governance
questions.explanation: PIM is an identity governance capability that needs Entra ID P2 or Entra ID Governance, including for users who are eligible for roles and group memberships.

questions.q: A user must perform an activation, optionally with MFA or approval, before a role takes effect. Which assignment type is this?
options: Active assignment
Permanent active assignment
Eligible assignment
Direct assignment outside PIM
questions.explanation: Eligible assignments require the member to activate the role before using it, while active assignments are usable immediately.

questions.q: Who is automatically assigned the Security Administrator and Privileged Role Administrator roles when PIM is first used in an organization?
options: The first person to use PIM
All Global Administrators
Every user with an Entra ID P2 license
Only the user who created the tenant
questions.explanation: Entra ID assigns Security Administrator and Privileged Role Administrator to the first person to use PIM in the organization.

questions.q: Which role is the least-privileged option for managing PIM role settings for a Microsoft Entra role?
options: Security Administrator
Security Reader
Authentication Policy Administrator
Privileged Role Administrator
questions.explanation: Managing PIM role settings for Entra roles requires at least Privileged Role Administrator.

questions.q: Which roles can read PIM security alerts for Microsoft Entra roles?
options: Only Global Administrator, Privileged Role Administrator and Security Administrator, because the reader roles are read-only
Global Administrator, Privileged Role Administrator, Global Reader, Security Administrator and Security Reader
Any user who has an eligible assignment
Only Security Administrator
questions.explanation: Those five roles can read the alerts, and managing the alert settings needs a role such as Privileged Role Administrator.

questions.q: An administrator changes the PIM role settings for the Exchange Administrator role. How does this affect other roles?
options: It applies to every role in the tenant, because role settings are tenant-wide policies for PIM
It applies to all roles in the same category
It applies to other roles that share the same permissions
It affects only that role, because role settings are defined per role and are independent
questions.explanation: Role settings, also called PIM policies, are defined for each role and don't affect other roles.

questions.q: Which kinds of Microsoft Entra roles can PIM manage?
options: Built-in roles only
Custom roles only
Both built-in and custom roles
Only roles with directory-level privileges
questions.explanation: PIM supports built-in and custom Microsoft Entra roles.

questions.q: What is the allowed range for the activation maximum duration of a role in PIM?
options: From 15 minutes to 8 hours
From one to 72 hours
From one to 24 hours
From one day to 30 days
questions.explanation: The activation maximum duration slider accepts values from one to 24 hours.

questions.q: Administrators activate roles from a device on which they signed in with Windows Hello for Business. You want them to authenticate again with a different method at activation. What should you configure?
options: Require a Conditional Access authentication context together with an authentication strength
On activation, require multifactor authentication only, because Windows Hello for Business always counts as MFA
Require ticket information on activation
Require justification on activation
questions.explanation: The MFA setting may be satisfied by earlier strong authentication in the session. An authentication context with an authentication strength forces a specific method at activation.

questions.q: You configure On activation, require Conditional Access authentication context for a role. Which statement is correct?
options: The policy should target the directory role and the authentication context at the same time so that it applies during and after activation
The policy should target the authentication context for eligible users, not the directory role at the same time, and it should exist before you configure PIM
The policy can be in report-only mode and is still enforced
PIM falls back to MFA even if the policy is turned off
questions.explanation: During activation the user doesn't have the role yet, so a policy that targets the role doesn't apply. The MFA backup applies only when no policy targets the context, and not when the policy is off, report-only or excludes the user.

questions.q: You must force users to reauthenticate every time they activate a role. How?
options: Set the activation maximum duration to one hour and require justification and ticket information on activation
Require ticket information on activation
Require approval with two approvers
Use a Conditional Access policy for the authentication context with sign-in frequency set to Every time
questions.explanation: Sign-in frequency set to Every time in the Conditional Access policy that targets the authentication context ensures reauthentication for each activation.

questions.q: A user reauthenticates to activate one eligible role and activates a second eligible role shortly afterward. What applies?
options: A 10-minute window applies across Entra roles, Azure resource roles and PIM for Groups, so no new prompt appears within it
A 60-minute window applies to Entra roles only, and Azure resource roles always prompt again
Every activation always prompts again
The window applies only to roles in the same category
questions.explanation: After a reauthentication for one activation, other activations within 10 minutes don't prompt again, regardless of whether they are Entra roles, Azure roles or group memberships.

questions.q: What does the Require ticket information on activation setting do?
options: It asks for a ticket number, but the value isn't validated against any ticketing system
It validates the number against ServiceNow or another ticketing system automatically before activation
It requires an approver to enter the ticket
It opens a ticket in the Microsoft 365 admin center
questions.explanation: The ticket field is informational only, and PIM doesn't correlate it with information in a ticketing system.

questions.q: Auditors need to know why administrators activate privileged roles. What should you enable in the role settings?
options: Require justification on active assignment
Allow permanent eligible assignment
Require justification on activation
Send notifications to the activated user only
questions.explanation: Justification on activation captures the business reason each time an eligible user activates. The active assignment version applies when an admin creates an active assignment.

questions.q: You require approval to activate a role but don't select any approvers. Who become the default approvers?
options: The user's manager
Security Administrators
The group owners of the activating user and any member of the Security Administrator role
Active Privileged Role Administrators and Global Administrators
questions.explanation: If no approvers are selected, active Privileged Role Administrators and Global Administrators become the default approvers.

questions.q: Which combination can lock you out of your tenant?
options: All Privileged Role Administrators and Global Administrators are eligible only, approval is required, and no approvers are configured
Approval is required, and two specific approvers are configured
Emergency access accounts have permanent active Global Administrator assignments
One Global Administrator exists and is permanently active
questions.explanation: If nobody can activate and approvals have no configured approvers, nobody can approve a request. Emergency access accounts and specific approvers prevent this.

questions.q: How many approvers does Microsoft recommend selecting for role activation approval?
options: Exactly one
At least five
None; rely on the default approvers
At least two
questions.explanation: Select at least one approver and preferably two or more, so approvals don't depend on a single person. The approvers don't need to hold any role.

questions.q: Auditors require every eligible assignment to have a start and end date. Which setting meets this?
options: Allow permanent active assignment, which forces every assignment to have an end date
Require MFA on active assignment
Expire eligible assignment after, instead of Allow permanent eligible assignment
An activation maximum duration of one hour
questions.explanation: The assignment duration settings decide whether eligible assignments can be permanent or must expire. Activation duration applies to each activation, not to the assignment.

questions.q: Why can't PIM enforce MFA when a user uses an active assignment?
options: MFA applies only to eligible users in the Free edition, and active assignments aren't covered by licensing
The user is already active in the role from the time it's assigned, so MFA applies only when the assignment is created
Active assignments use certificate-based authentication
MFA must be enforced by Conditional Access only for guests
questions.explanation: Require MFA on active assignment applies when the administrator creates the active assignment. PIM can't prompt when the user later uses a role that's already active.

questions.q: Which approach is recommended for emergency access accounts in a PIM deployment?
options: Make them eligible for Global Administrator with approval and exclude them from Conditional Access policies
Give them permanent active Global Administrator assignments and exclude them from Conditional Access policies
Require MFA on activation with a ticket number
Remove their role assignments and rely on approvals
questions.explanation: Emergency access accounts must work when other administrators can't activate, so they keep permanent active assignments and are excluded from policies that could block them.

questions.q: A user is assigned the Exchange Administrator role directly in Microsoft Entra, bypassing PIM. Which alert fires, and with what severity?
options: Potential stale accounts in a privileged role, severity Medium
There are too many Global Administrators, severity Low
Roles are being activated too frequently, severity Low
Roles are being assigned outside of Privileged Identity Management, severity High
questions.explanation: Assignments made outside PIM aren't monitored and might indicate an attack, so the alert has High severity.

questions.q: What is the severity of the Potential stale accounts in a privileged role alert?
options: High
Low
Medium
Informational
questions.explanation: Potential stale accounts is a Medium alert, the outside-of-PIM alert is High, and the remaining alerts are Low.

questions.q: The tenant has more Global Administrators than your policy allows. How can you tune the related alert?
options: Remove the alert from the PIM settings, because its thresholds can't be configured by administrators
Change the activation maximum duration
Require two approvers for Global Administrator
Adjust the thresholds for the number and percentage of Global Administrators in the alert settings
questions.explanation: The too-many-Global-Administrators alert has configurable thresholds, including the minimum percentage of administrators who are Global Administrators.

questions.q: What is the remedy for the alert Roles don't require multifactor authentication for activation?
options: Require approval on assignment
Require MFA on activation in the role settings
Enable a registration campaign
Turn on security defaults
questions.explanation: Without MFA, compromised users can activate privileged roles, so the fix is to enable the MFA requirement on activation for those roles.

questions.q: In PIM for Azure resources, which alerts have Medium severity?
options: Roles assigned outside PIM and potential stale accounts, plus roles that don't require MFA
Administrators aren't using their privileged roles
Too many owners assigned to a resource, and too many permanent owners assigned to a resource
Roles are being activated too frequently
questions.explanation: The Azure resource alerts for too many owners and too many permanent owners are Medium severity, and their emails go to Owners and User Access Administrators.

questions.q: Which PIM alert indicates possible misuse because the same role is activated repeatedly in a short period?
options: Potential stale accounts in a privileged role
Roles are being activated too frequently
Administrators aren't using their privileged roles
Roles don't require MFA for activation
questions.explanation: The too-frequent activation alert flags repeated activations that might mean the role is being used as a standing privilege or misused.

questions.q: Who has resource administrator permissions by default in PIM for Azure resources?
options: Only Global Administrators and Privileged Role Administrators who enabled subscription management
Owners and User Access Administrators of the subscription, and Global Administrators who enable subscription management
Contributors on the subscription
Security Administrators
questions.explanation: These administrators can assign roles, configure role settings and review access using PIM for Azure resources.

questions.q: Which feature lets you add conditions to eligible role assignments in PIM for Azure resources?
options: Conditional Access authentication context
Access packages
Azure attribute-based access control (Azure ABAC)
Administrative units
questions.explanation: Azure ABAC conditions can be added to eligible assignments for certain built-in roles in PIM for Azure resources.

questions.q: At which scopes can PIM manage Azure resource roles?
options: Management groups, subscriptions, resource groups and resources
Subscriptions only, because resource groups and resources can't be scoped in PIM
Tenants and management groups only
Only the tenant root
questions.explanation: PIM for Azure resources starts at a management group or subscription and can go down to resource groups and resources.

questions.q: Which Azure roles can PIM manage?
options: Only Owner and User Access Administrator
Only built-in roles
Only custom roles
Built-in and custom Azure roles
questions.explanation: PIM supports both built-in and custom Azure roles, including Owner, User Access Administrator, Contributor and others.

questions.q: A user will be an eligible member of a group in PIM for Groups. What is required for that user?
options: A Microsoft 365 E3 license
A Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra ID Governance license
Membership in an administrative unit
The Groups Administrator role
questions.explanation: Every user who is eligible for membership or ownership of a PIM for Groups needs P2 or Governance.

questions.q: You aren't the owner of a role-assignable group. Which role is the minimum to make users eligible members in PIM for Groups?
options: Groups Administrator
User Administrator
Privileged Role Administrator
Identity Governance Administrator
questions.explanation: For role-assignable groups you need at least Privileged Role Administrator or must own the group.

questions.q: Who can assign eligibility for a non-role-assignable group in PIM for Groups?
options: Directory Writers, Groups Administrators, Identity Governance Administrators, User Administrators, or the group's owner
Only Global Administrators
Only Privileged Role Administrators and Global Administrators, because group roles aren't delegable
Only the group's members
questions.explanation: Non-role-assignable groups can be managed by those roles or by the group's owner. Role-assignable groups need at least Privileged Role Administrator or ownership.

questions.q: Group A is an eligible member of Group B, and Ann is an active member of Group A. What can Ann do?
options: Group A is automatically a member of Group B
Activate membership in Group B, but Group A doesn't become a member of Group B
Nothing; nesting isn't supported in PIM for Groups
All members of Group A become members of Group B immediately
questions.explanation: One group can be an eligible member of another, and activation applies to the user who requested it.

questions.q: Which statement about role-assignable groups used with PIM is correct?
options: They must use dynamic membership, so that role assignments follow user attributes
Role-assignable groups can't have other groups nested as active members
They can be nested in other role-assignable groups as active members
They don't need Entra ID P2
questions.explanation: Role-assignable groups can't nest other groups, which keeps role assignments easy to audit.

questions.q: A role assignment with an end date is about to expire. Who can renew it for others, and what happens to user-initiated extension requests?
options: Global Administrators and Privileged Role Administrators can renew, and user-initiated extension or renewal requests need their approval
Any eligible user can renew their own assignment without approval, up to the assignment's maximum duration
Security Administrators can renew all assignments
Assignments renew automatically if the user activated them
questions.explanation: Users can request an extension or renewal, and Global Administrators or Privileged Role Administrators approve it. Those admins can also renew assignments themselves.

questions.q: You want PIM to email recipients only about events that need immediate action. Which notification option fits?
options: Critical emails only
Turn off all emails
Send emails to default recipients only
Add additional recipients
questions.explanation: With Critical emails only, PIM continues to send emails only when immediate action is required, such as approving an extension request.

questions.q: Where do users activate their eligible Microsoft Entra roles?
options: In Roles and administrators by editing their assignment
In the Access Reviews blade
In Privileged Identity Management, under My roles
In Entitlement management, under Access packages
questions.explanation: Eligible users open PIM and activate the role from My roles, supplying MFA, justification or ticket information if required.

questions.q: Contractors need the Application Administrator role for exactly two weeks starting next Monday. How should this be assigned in PIM?
options: As a permanent active assignment
Through an access review of the role
As a permanent eligible assignment
As an eligible or active assignment with a custom start date and end date
questions.explanation: PIM supports time-bound assignments with start and end dates, so the access ends automatically.

questions.q: Helpdesk staff should receive Helpdesk Administrator only when needed, with approval. How should you implement this by using PIM for Groups?
options: Create a role-assignable group, assign the role to the group, and make the staff eligible members with approval required
Create a dynamic group that has the role assigned, and make the staff active members so that the role follows their department
Assign the role directly and require approval on the active assignment
Create an administrative unit that is scoped to the staff
questions.explanation: A role-assignable group holds the role, and PIM for Groups gives eligible members just-in-time access with approval. Active assignments and dynamic groups don't provide just-in-time access.
